newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: San Teh offers warrants, in US$38 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: San Teh offers warrants, in US$38 mln loan.

text.p: Rubber keypad maker San Teh Ltd said on Friday it planned to offer 38 million warrants for 38 million new ordinary shares of Singapore $0.20 each.
This is in conjunction with a US$38 million transferable loan facility, it said in a statement.
San Teh said the purpose was to raise medium term funds at a favourable interest rate to support expansion plans.
The company said it expected to net about US$37.4 million from the issue which would be used to expand its cement plant in China's Fujian province and to repay bank borrowings.
Pending the deployment of the issue's proceeds, San Teh said it might deposit the funds with financial institutions or use them to invest in various money market or debt instruments.
San Teh said 150 warrants would be offered for every 1,000 ordinary shares held.
The connected loan facility would be for a term of five years subject to option by the lenders to have it repaid in full in three years.
It said the new shares issued upon the exercise of the warrants would rank pari passu in all respects with existing ordinary shares.
The warrants and loan, to be approved by the SES and shareholders, would be handled by OCBC Bank Ltd.
